facts.claim: The prompt phase reads the whole prompt at once, so its work can be parallelised with matrix-matrix multiplication and uses the GPU efficiently (Kwon et al., 2023, the vLLM paper).
The generation phase writes new tokens one at a time, mostly with matrix-vector multiplication; it underuses the GPU’s compute and is memory-bound (Kwon et al., 2023).
Batching several requests improves a server’s use of its compute, because the cost of moving the weights is shared by every request in the batch (Kwon et al., 2023).
OPT-13B, an open model with 13 billion parameters, has 40 layers, 40 attention heads and a hidden size (d_model) of 5,120, stored as 16-bit floats, and reads up to 2,048 tokens.
For OPT-13B, the KV cache of a single token takes 800 KB: 2 (key and value) × 5,120 × 40 layers × 2 bytes. A request of 2,048 tokens can need 1.6 GB (Kwon et al., 2023).
Serving a 13-billion-parameter model on an NVIDIA A100 with 40 GB, about 65% of the memory holds the weights and close to 30% holds the requests’ KV cache (Kwon et al., 2023).
In the serving systems the vLLM authors profiled, only 20.4% to 38.2% of the KV cache memory held actual token states; the rest was lost to reservation and fragmentation.

PagedAttention stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks, like pages in an operating system, so memory is not reserved up front; vLLM, built on it, improves throughput 2–4× at the same latency (Kwon et al., 2023).

Orca introduced iteration-level scheduling: the server schedules one model iteration at a time, so finished requests leave the batch and new ones join between iterations. On GPT-3 175B it reported 36.9× the throughput of NVIDIA FasterTransformer at the same latency (Yu et al., OSDI 2022).
GPTQ quantizes the weights of a 175-billion-parameter GPT model to 3 or 4 bits in about four GPU hours, with negligible loss of accuracy (Frantar et al., ICLR 2023).
AWQ quantizes weights only, to low bits, and finds that protecting just 1% of salient weights, chosen by looking at the activations, greatly reduces the error (Lin et al., 2023).

DistServe counts a request as served well only when it meets both a first-token target and a per-token target; planned for both, it served up to 7.4× more requests than earlier systems with over 90% of requests on target (Zhong et al., OSDI 2024).
For a chatbot on OPT-13B, DistServe’s authors set the first-token target to 0.25 s and the per-token target to 0.1 s, faster than people read (Zhong et al., 2024).

Speculative decoding computes several tokens in parallel by checking a smaller model’s guesses with the large one, without any change to the outputs; on T5-XXL it ran 2–3× faster with identical outputs (Leviathan et al., 2023).

Speculative sampling scores a faster draft model’s short continuations with the target model in parallel; with Chinchilla 70B it decoded 2–2.5× faster, and its rejection scheme keeps the target model’s distribution (Chen et al., 2023).
